title: Professional Services Contract - Linda Grundhoffer - Chief Systems and Services Officer
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Linda Grundhoffer, Danville, CA, for the latter to provide support with the FY18/19 Unaudited Actuals, FY18/19 Audit, processing payroll and guiding the Accounting Staff in closing processes, coordinating closing tasks and assignments, preparing, reviewing, and approving closing entries and items, via Chief Systems and Services Officer, for the term August 1, 2019 through October 31, 2019, in an amount not to exceed $18,000.00.
headline: Pays a finance contractor up to $18,000 for year-end audit, payroll and closing support
summary: The district hires an outside contractor from Danville to help with last year's unaudited financial figures and audit, run payroll, and guide accounting staff through closing the books. The contract runs August 1 through October 31, 2019, and is capped at $18,000.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
title: Agreement for Architectural Services - Shah Kawasaki Architects - Cole Administration Center Project
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 1920-2024 - Award of Contract for Architectural Services for the Cole Administration Center Project to Shah Kawasaki Architects, Oakland, CA, as the selected contractor, in the amount of Three Million, Five Hundred Thousand dollars 00/100 ($3,500,000.00), and authorizing the President and Secretary of the Board to sign the Agreement with said Architect with work scheduled to commence on September 12, 2019, and to last until December 31, 2022, pursuant to the terms and conditions of the Contract.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Awards Shah Kawasaki Architects $3.5M to design the Cole Administration Center project
summary: The Board awards the architectural design contract for the Cole Administration Center project to Shah Kawasaki Architects of Oakland, for $3,500,000. Work starts September 12, 2019 and runs until December 31, 2022. It is paid from Measure J bond funds.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
title: Amendment No. 1, Contract for Services - Star Elevator - McClymonds High School
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Contract (Agreement) for Services between the District and Star Elevator, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide labor and materials to perform emergency repairs on the passenger elevator at McClymonds High School, in an amount not to exceed $7,537.62, increasing existing Contract, for the term March 14, 2019 through December 31, 2019, with vendor not to exceed amount from $34,688.90 to $42,226.52. All other terms and conditions of the Contract (Agreement) remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $7,537.62 for Star Elevator's emergency elevator repairs at McClymonds High

It raises the contract limit from $34,688.90 to $42,226.52. The contract period began March 14, 2019, before this approval, and runs through December 31, 2019.

group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management

group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
title: Award of Contract for Construction Services – Non Competitively Bid – Alaniz Construction, Inc. – Washington (Sankofa) Finishing Kitchen Project - Facilities Planning & Management Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 1920-0021 - Award of Contract for Construction Services for the Washington (Sankofa) Finishing Kitchen Project [Non-Bid Award] to Alaniz Construction, Inc., Oakland, CA, as the selected contractor, in the amount of $37,212.00, for labor and materials to repair existing parking lot pavement, and authorizing the President and Secretary of the Board to sign the Agreement with said contractor with work scheduled to commence on August 8, 2019, and scheduled to last until August 10, 2019, pursuant to the terms and conditions of the Contract.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management

summary: The Board awards Alaniz Construction, Inc. of Oakland $37,212 for labor and materials to repair existing parking lot pavement as part of the Washington (Sankofa) Finishing Kitchen project. The contract was not competitively bid. The work was scheduled for August 8 through August 10, 2019, before this approval.

group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
title: Award of Contract for Construction Services – Non Competitively Bid – Rook Electric - Various Security Improvements and Repair Project – Facilities Planning & Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 1920-0017 -  Award  of Contract for Construction Services for The Various Security Improvements & Repair Project [Non-Bid Award) to Rook Electric, Oakland, CA,  as the selected contractor. for performance of work described in the Scope of Work in the Contract, i.e., repairs and or installation of security equipment, as described in attached invoices in the cumulative amount of $20,950.00, and authorizing the President and Secretary of the Board to sign the Agreement for same with said contractor for payment only on work which was performed from May 1, 2019 through May 17, 2019.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Pays Rook Electric $20,950 for security equipment work done in May 2019, without bidding
summary: The Board approves payment of $20,950 to Rook Electric of Oakland for repairs and installation of security equipment, as listed on attached invoices. The agreement covers payment only for work already performed from May 1 through May 17, 2019. The contract was not competitively bid.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost - Teach for America - Community Partnerships - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost between the District and Teach for America, New York, NY, for the latter to provide five weeks of teacher training including four weeks of teaching summer school covering the following content areas: elementary reading, elementary writing, elementary math, secondary ELA, secondary math, and secondary science, at Roosevelt Middle School, for the period of January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2021, at no cost to the District.
headline: Accepts Teach for America's free teacher training and summer school at Roosevelt Middle
summary: This no-cost memorandum of understanding (a partnership agreement) lets Teach for America provide five weeks of teacher training, including four weeks of teaching summer school, at Roosevelt Middle School. Subjects include elementary reading, writing and math, and secondary English, math and science. It runs January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2021 at no cost to the district.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost - Alexis Lavine-Moore - Community Partnerships - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost between the District and Alexis Lavine-Moore, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide a series of gardening classes where students will enjoy hands-on learning of biology and ecology, and will gain understanding of food sources and how to nurture, respect, and enjoy them, at Thornhill Elementary School, for the period of August 12, 2019 through August 12, 2022, at no cost to the District.
headline: Accepts free gardening classes for Thornhill Elementary students through August 2022
summary: This no-cost memorandum of understanding (a partnership agreement) has a local provider teach a series of gardening classes at Thornhill Elementary School. Students learn hands-on biology and ecology and where food comes from. It runs August 12, 2019 through August 12, 2022 at no cost to the district.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Rene Ernesto Quinonez - English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Rene Ernesto Quinonez, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide safety intervention and youth development services program for newcomer students, as described in the Scope of Work, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department, for the period of August 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $66,200.00.
headline: Ratifies a contract up to $66,200 for safety and youth development help for newcomer students
summary: The Board approves, after the start date, a contract with an Oakland contractor to run a safety intervention and youth development program for newcomer students, through the English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department. It runs August 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020 and is capped at $66,200.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Educational Organization Contract Re Field Trips - Cazadero Performing Arts Camp - Various District Schools
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Educational Organization Contract Re Field Trips between the District and Cazadero Performing Arts Camp, Berkeley, CA, for the latter to provide participating music students from middle schools, with assistance from student high school mentors, its outdoor music education camps, entitled “Jump Start In Music” and “Summer Music Camp” occurring from September 15, 2019 through September 15, 2022, at no cost to the District.
headline: Accepts free music camps from Cazadero Performing Arts Camp for middle school students
summary: Cazadero Performing Arts Camp will offer its "Jump Start In Music" and "Summer Music Camp" outdoor music camps to participating middle school music students, with high school student mentors helping. The camps run from September 15, 2019 through September 15, 2022 at no cost to the district.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Syntex Global, Inc. - Special Education Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Syntex Global, Inc., San Francisco , CA, for the latter to provide additional or supplemental translators in Arabic, Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese, Cambodian, or other languages, as needed, if available, upon the District's request, when District’s need exceeds capacity or availability of employee translators to provide translation services, and to provide technical support for interpreting and translating that is legally required for Individualized Education Program (IEP) meetings via Special Education Department, for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020 in an amount not to exceed $65,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $65,000 for Syntex Global translators at special education meetings
summary: Syntex Global, Inc. provides extra translators in Arabic, Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese, Cambodian and other languages when district staff translators are not enough. This includes legally required translation for Individualized Education Program (IEP) meetings. The contract runs July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, is capped at $65,000, and began before Board approval.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Adkinstrak Timing Associates - Oakland Athletic League (OAL)
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Adkinstrak Timing Associates, Vallejo, CA, for the latter to provide customized timing solutions to track and field and cross country meets for students, via the Oakland Athletic League (OAL), for the period of September 2, 2019 through May 27, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $6,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $6,000 for Adkinstrak Timing to time track and cross country meets
summary: Adkinstrak Timing Associates of Vallejo provides customized timing for track and field and cross country meets through the Oakland Athletic League. The contract runs September 2, 2019 through May 27, 2020 and is capped at $6,000. It began before Board approval.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - HERO - Horace Mann Elementary School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and HERO, Oakland, CA, for the latter to furnish a coach who will provide organized games and physical activities; the Young Hero Leadership Program for upper grade students; and a variety of counseling and mentoring services at Horace Mann Elementary School, for the period of August 12, 2019, through May 28, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $30,000.00.

headline: Ratifies up to $30,000 for HERO coaching and mentoring at Horace Mann Elementary
summary: HERO of Oakland provides a coach for organized games and physical activities, the Young Hero Leadership Program for upper grade students, and counseling and mentoring at Horace Mann Elementary School. The contract runs August 12, 2019 through May 28, 2020 and is capped at $30,000. It began before Board approval.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - HERO - Garfield Elementary School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and HERO, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide a variety of mentoring and leadership services to students including a young HERO leadership program for upper grade students twice a week, Physical Education support and recess support in the form of organized games and physical activities for all grade levels at Garfield Elementary School, for the period of September 3, 2019 through May 28, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $27,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $27,000 for HERO mentoring, leadership and recess support at Garfield Elementary
summary: HERO of Oakland provides mentoring and leadership services at Garfield Elementary School, including a Young HERO leadership program for upper grade students twice a week, plus physical education and recess support for all grades. The contract runs September 3, 2019 through May 28, 2020 and is capped at $27,000. It began before Board approval.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - HERO - Parker Elementary School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and HERO, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide a variety of counseling/ mentoring services to target student population - Title I, Latino, African American and Second Language students - in the form of Social Skills Lessons, Leadership Program, Mentoring, Professional Development, and Organized Recess, as described in the Scope of Work, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, at Parker Elementary School, for the period of August 12, 2019 through May 28, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $30,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $30,000 for HERO counseling, mentoring and recess programs at Parker Elementary
summary: HERO of Oakland provides counseling and mentoring for Title I, Latino, African American and second-language students at Parker Elementary School. Services include social skills lessons, a leadership program, mentoring, professional development and organized recess. The contract runs August 12, 2019 through May 28, 2020, is capped at $30,000, and began before Board approval.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Subcontract - Spanish Speaking Unity Council - General Child Care and Development Programs - Early Childhood Education
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 1920-0154 - Authorizing Subcontract To The Spanish Speaking Unity Council, A Private Not-For-Profit Child Development Agency, A Portion Of The Oakland Unified School District's Fiscal Year 2019-20 Child Development Funding, (California Department of Education, Grant Contract No. CCTR-9010, Project Number 01-6125-00-9, for the Early Childhood Education Department), for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $450,000.00, with an administrative fee in the amount of $33,750.00 payable by the City to the District.
funding_source: California Department of Education, CCTR-9010 Grant
headline: Subcontracts up to $450,000 of child care funding to the Spanish Speaking Unity Council
summary: The district passes part of its 2019-20 state child development grant to the Spanish Speaking Unity Council, a private nonprofit child development agency, for up to $450,000. The text also lists a $33,750 administrative fee payable to the district. The period is July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020.
source_issue: The action text names the Spanish Speaking Unity Council as the subcontractor but says the administrative fee is payable by "the City" to the District, leaving unclear which party pays the fee.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Subcontract - City of Oakland - Head Start Program - Early Childhood Education
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 1920-0155 - Authorizing Subcontracting To The City Of Oakland, Nonprofit Public Benefit Corporation, Thru Its Child Development Agency, A Portion Of The Oakland Unified School District's Fiscal Year 2019-20 Child Development Funding, (utilizing the California Department of Education, Grant Contract No. CCTR-9010, Project Number 01-6125-00-9, for the Early Childhood Education Department), for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $250,000.00, with the City paying the District an earned administrative fee of 7.5% of the Contract Amount.

summary: The district passes part of its 2019-20 state child development grant to the City of Oakland, through its Child Development Agency, for up to $250,000. The City pays the district an earned administrative fee of 7.5% of the contract amount. The period is July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost - Jenelle McBride dba Study Buddy - Community Partnerships - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Memorandum of Understanding, No Cost between the District and Jenelle McBride dba Study Buddy, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide after school study sessions for students that focus on various academic needs in math, reading and writing, with collaboration between provider, teachers and parents at Redwood Heights Elementary School, for the period of August 5, 2019 through August 5, 2022, at no cost to the District.
headline: Accepts free after-school study sessions from Study Buddy at Redwood Heights Elementary
summary: This no-cost memorandum of understanding (a partnership agreement) has Study Buddy provide after-school study sessions at Redwood Heights Elementary School. Sessions focus on math, reading and writing, with the provider working with teachers and parents. It runs August 5, 2019 through August 5, 2022 at no cost to the district.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Teri Smith - Oakland International High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Teri Smith, Oakland, CA, for the latter to supervise counseling interns, attend COST meetings and partner meetings throughout the school year, at Oakland International High School, for the period of August 12, 2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $25,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $25,000 for a contractor to supervise counseling interns at Oakland International High
summary: An Oakland contractor supervises counseling interns and attends student support team and partner meetings at Oakland International High School. The contract runs August 12, 2019 through June 30, 2020 and is capped at $25,000. It began before Board approval.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Nonpublic, Nonsectarian School/Agency Services Master Contract(s) - 2019-2020 School Year - Special Education Program
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution Number 1920-0151 - New Master Agreements or Contracts and Individual Service Agreements with Non-Public, Nonsectarian School/Agency Services for students of Special Education Program for Fiscal Year 2019-2020 in a cumulative amount not to exceed $22,000,000.00.
headline: Authorizes up to $22M in 2019-20 contracts with nonpublic schools and agencies for special education
summary: This resolution approves new master agreements and individual service agreements with nonpublic, nonsectarian schools and agencies that serve students in the special education program. The total for all of them is capped at $22,000,000 for the 2019-20 fiscal year. The text does not name the individual schools or agencies.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Subaward Agreement - Strategic Education Research Partnership (SERP) Institute - (Extension of Time) - Academics and Instructional Innovation Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, SubAward Agreement between the District and Strategic Education Research Partnership Institute (SERP), Washington, DC, for the latter to support development of a year-long high school chemistry curriculum, as described herein, and accepting associated $80,000.00 grant award therefor, from the Koshland Foundation, pursuant to terms and conditions thereof, extending the term of the SubAward Agreement from October 1, 2018 through July 31, 2019 to July 31, 2020.  All other terms and conditions of the SubAward Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Extends SERP's chemistry curriculum work to July 2020; memo cites $80,000 in Koshland grant funding
summary: This amendment extends the agreement with the Strategic Education Research Partnership Institute (SERP), which is helping develop a year-long high school chemistry curriculum, from July 31, 2019 to July 31, 2020. The amendment document itself changes only the term. The district memo cites $80,000 in Koshland Foundation grant funding for the part-time science specialist, and the grant award letter lists $80,000 for the 2019-20 school year, so this appears to be the next year's installment rather than a restatement, though the documents do not say so outright.
source_issue: The official text accepts an $80,000 grant award in an item titled as an extension of time, without saying whether it is new money or the original grant restated; the signed amendment itself changes only the term.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - First Alarm Security & Patrol - Police Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and First Alarm Security & Patrol, San Jose, CA, for the latter to respond to Alarms and monitoring of sites when District Police Services Officers are off duty including District Holidays and weekends, as specified in Agreement, via Police Services Department, for the period of July 22, 2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $165,000.00.
headline: Pays First Alarm Security & Patrol up to $165,000 for alarm response and off-hours site monitoring
summary: First Alarm Security & Patrol of San Jose responds to alarms and monitors district sites when District Police Services officers are off duty, including holidays and weekends. The contract runs July 22, 2019 through June 30, 2020 and is capped at $165,000.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Side Letter Agreement - District and Oakland Education Association (“OEA”) - National Education Association (''NEA'") Community Schools Grant - Release Time
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Side Letter of Agreement, as Agreement between the District and the Oakland Education Association (“OEA”), regarding  the  National  Education  Association  (''NEA'") Community  Schools Grant and release time for OEA leadership participation, in particular providing for the release of teacher, Kampala Taiz-Rancifer, for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, pursuant to terms and conditions thereof, with the Agreement (Side Letter) in effect between the Parties from July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022.
headline: Approves a side agreement with the teachers union on release time for a National Education Association grant
summary: The district and the Oakland Education Association (OEA), the teachers union, sign a side letter about the National Education Association (NEA) Community Schools Grant. It gives a teacher release time from the classroom to take part in OEA leadership, for July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020. The side letter itself stays in effect through June 30, 2022. The text states no dollar amount.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract - Board on Track - Charter Schools Office
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Board on Track, Concord, MA, for the latter to assist the Office of Charter Schools (OCS) with appointments to charter boards as required by Board Resolution 1718-0168; develop video training modules to be used to train appointees to charter boards on the requirements and best practices of their position; provide OCS with thought partnership and support to OCS staff on designing reporting materials and matching applicants to charter boards; and in June 2020, provide selected boards with a skill appraisal to help OCS evaluate the skill set of board, via the Office of Charter Schools, for the period of July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $45,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $45,000 for Board on Track to support charter school board appointments
summary: Board on Track of Concord, Massachusetts helps the Office of Charter Schools with appointments to charter school boards. It builds video training modules for appointees, advises staff on reporting materials and applicant matching, and gives selected boards a skills appraisal in June 2020. The contract runs July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020 and is capped at $45,000. It began before Board approval.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Redesignation of Recognition Date - District's 2019-2020 Teacher(s) of the Year - Board of Education
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 1819-0093A - Redesignation of Date of Recognition of Oakland Unified School District’s 2019-2020 Teacher of the Year.
headline: Changes the date for recognizing the district's 2019-2020 Teacher of the Year
summary: This resolution sets a new date for the Board to recognize the Oakland Unified School District's 2019-2020 Teacher of the Year. The text does not state the new date or any cost.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
